enonce.texte:
Read the following descriptions of communication styles and match them with the correct cultural context.

Communication Styles:

  • A. Direct Communication: People say exactly what they mean. Honesty and clarity are valued. Silence is often uncomfortable.
  • B. Indirect Communication: People imply meaning rather than stating it directly. Context and nonverbal cues are important. Silence can be a sign of respect.
  • C. High-Context Communication: Much of the message is understood through shared knowledge, relationships, and nonverbal cues.
  • D. Low-Context Communication: The message is explicit and detailed. People rely on words rather than context.
images: A simple diagram showing a spectrum from 'Direct/Low-context' to 'Indirect/High-context' with flags of USA, UK, Germany on the left and Japan, China, Arab countries on the right.

questions.texte: Match each scenario with the most appropriate communication style (A, B, C, or D).

sousQuestions.texte: A British manager gives very clear instructions step by step.
An American colleague says, 'Let's cut to the chase. What's the bottom line?'
A Japanese employee says, 'That might be difficult' to mean 'No, I can't do that.'
A Cameroonian family understands a gesture or a look without any words being spoken.

enonce.texte:
Read the dialogue between a French manager and a Cameroonian employee, then answer the questions.

Dialogue:

Manager (French): 'Your report is late again. You need to respect deadlines. It's very simple: deliver on time.'

Employee (Cameroonian): 'Yes, sir. I understand. But there was a problem with the internet and I had to wait for my colleague to send me the data.'

Manager: 'That's not an excuse. You should have anticipated this. Next time, I want the report on Friday at 5 PM sharp.'

Employee: 'I will do my best, boss.'

Manager (to a colleague): 'He's not taking responsibility. He's making excuses.'

Employee (to a colleague): 'The boss is very harsh. He doesn't understand that we have to work with the community and people aren't always available. He doesn't respect our way of doing things.'
images: A split illustration showing a French person checking a watch and a Cameroonian person greeting elders in a village, highlighting different perceptions of time.

questions.texte: Analyse the dialogue and identify at least two cultural misunderstandings.
questions.reponse: 1) Perception of time (monochronic vs polychronic), 2) Direct vs indirect communication, 3) Power distance (hierarchy vs egalitarianism)

sousQuestions.texte: How does the manager perceive the employee's explanation?
sousQuestions.reponse: The manager sees it as an excuse and a lack of responsibility, focusing on the deadline.

sousQuestions.texte: How does the employee perceive the manager's feedback?
sousQuestions.reponse: The employee sees it as harsh and unempathetic, not understanding the challenges of his work environment.

sousQuestions.texte: Propose a better way for the manager to communicate his expectations.
sousQuestions.reponse: A better approach would be: 'I understand you faced challenges. How can we work together to ensure future deadlines are met? Could we set up a weekly check-in to anticipate problems?' This shows empathy while maintaining accountability.

intitule: Practical Application in a Multicultural Meeting

enonce.texte:
You are working on an international project team with members from Cameroon, the UK, and India. You need to propose a new schedule. The UK team member is very direct and wants a clear timeline. The Indian team member is indirect and values harmony. The Cameroonian team member emphasizes relationships and flexibility.

Your task: Write a brief script of what you would say to introduce the new schedule in a way that respects all three communication styles.

questions.texte: Write your script. Make sure to address all three styles (minimum 10 lines).
questions.reponse:
Exemple de réponse: 'Good morning everyone. Thank you for being here. I've been thinking about our schedule and I'd like to propose a new approach.

To my UK colleague, I know you appreciate clarity, so I've prepared a detailed timeline with specific dates and milestones.

To my Indian colleague, I value your input and I'm open to adjusting this plan so that everyone is comfortable with it. Your perspective on team harmony is very important.

To my Cameroonian colleague, I've made sure there is some flexibility because I know that building strong relationships with our partners is key. We can adapt as needed.

So here is a draft. I'd like us to discuss it openly, but also with respect for each other's time and contributions. What do you all think?'

enonce.texte:
Original Email (from a French manager to a Cameroonian team):

Subject: Urgent - New Policy Implementation

Dear Team,

As you know, the new policy must be implemented by next Monday. I expect all of you to have completed the training by then. There is no excuse for non-compliance. Please send me your confirmation by Friday.

Best regards,

Manager
images: A mock email inbox with the above email displayed, highlighting the harsh tone.

questions.texte: Revise the email to make it more culturally appropriate for a Cameroonian audience while maintaining clarity.
questions.reponse:
Subject: Training Completion and New Policy

Dear Team,

I hope you are all doing well. I'm writing to remind you about the new policy and the required training.

I understand that everyone has busy schedules, and some colleagues may need additional support to complete the training. Please let me know if you encounter any difficulties.

The deadline for completion is next Monday. Could you please let me know by Friday if you are on track? Also, if you have any questions or suggestions, feel free to reach out to me or to HR.

Your cooperation is much appreciated, and I am confident that we can do this together as a team.

Best regards,

Manager

enonce.texte:
Read the following statements and identify the cross-cultural communication barrier they illustrate. Choose from:

  • A. Ethnocentrism
  • B. Stereotyping
  • C. Language barriers
  • D. Nonverbal misinterpretation

questions.texte: Classify each statement (1 to 4) with the correct barrier (A, B, C, or D).

sousQuestions.texte: 'All British people are reserved and unfriendly.'
'Our way of doing business is the only right way. If they don't follow it, they are wrong.'
A French phrase like 'rendez-vous' is used, but the Cameroonian employee doesn't understand the formal connotation.
A Cameroonian nods to show he is listening, but the American interprets it as agreement.

enonce.texte:
You are a Cameroonian professional welcoming a British business partner. Describe how you would greet them in a way that is respectful of Cameroonian culture but also comfortable for the British partner.

Include: verbal greetings, body language, and possible small talk topics.
images: A Cameroonian person shaking hands with a British person while smiling, with a background of a modern office.

questions.reponse:
Verbal: 'Good morning! Welcome to Cameroon. I hope you had a good flight.' or in French 'Bonjour! Bienvenue au Cameroun.'
Body language: A firm handshake with a smile, maybe with the left hand supporting the right elbow as a sign of respect.
Small talk: Ask about the flight, the weather, or if they have been to Cameroon before. Avoid political topics or anything too personal. Show genuine interest in their comfort.
